description: Anchored means the engine tied a finding to the surface it enumerated (ADR-009), and it is what decides whether a finding fails a build. Several analyses assert it by construction, on the sound reasoning that a weak key in a file nothing routes to is still a weak key -- but `nothing routes to it` and `nothing can run it` are different facts and the second one was never asked. An application reported the `window.open` inside a settings button at error level, gating, on the strength of a handler local to the component, and the component is not imported, re-exported or dynamically loaded anywhere in its own repository: there is no path from any enumerated entry point down to that line. Five findings here and all five are reported, because the code says what it says; what the two in unreferenced modules lose is the claim about WHERE they are -- the same correction the surface made when it started printing `<unresolved:expr>` for a mount path it could not read instead of `*`. The three that keep it are the reason this cannot be done by suppressing anything: a module the process entry imports, a module a page imports, and the page itself, which nothing imports and never would because the framework loads it by PATH. Anchoring is asserted in `anchoring_test.go`, since it is not expressible as a finding -- which is exactly how it was wrong.

expected.note: reached from the process entry, so the finding stands where the engine puts it
the identical call in a module nothing names. Still reported -- the IV is written down either way -- and no longer claiming to stand on the surface
nothing imports a page and nothing ever would: the framework loads it by path, and reading `no import` as `no caller` here would be a statement about the framework rather than about the program
the same call as the orphan below, in a component the page imports. The difference between the two is the whole judgement
the shape the corpus exists for: a component-local handler was enough to gate a build on a component nothing in the tree renders
